div.l: A long surcote of peers vpon he hadde
And by his syde he bare a rusty bladde
Of Norffolk was this Reve of whom I telle
By syden̄ a toun̄ men cleped it Baldeswelle
Tukked he was as is a frere a boute
And eủer he rode the hyndrest of our route
A somynoᵘur was ther with vs in that place
That hadde a fyry cherubynez face
For Sawceleūn he was with eyen narwe
As hoot he was and lecherous as a sparwe
With scalled browes blak and pylled berde
Of hise visage children weren a ferde
Ther ne was quykke sylủer litarge ne brensten̄
Boras Ceruse ne oyle of tartre non̄
Ne onyment that wolde clense and byte
That hym myght helpe of whelkys white
Nor of the knobbys sittyng in his chekys
Weel loved he garlek onyons and eke lekys
And for to drynk strong wyn rede as blood
Thanne wolde he speke and crye as he wer wood
And whan þat he weel dronken had the wyne
Thanne wold he speke no woord but latyne
A fewe termes had he two or three
That he had lerned out of som decree
No wonder is he herd it all the daye
And eke ye knowe it weel how that a Iaye
Can clepe wat as weel as can the pope
But who so coude in other thyng hym grope
Thanne had he spente all hise philosophye
. Ay questio quid iuris wold he crye
He was a genty harlot and a kynde
A better felawe shuld men nat fynde
He wolde suffre for a quarte of wyne
A gode felow to haue hise concubyne
A twelfmoneth and excuse hym at þe fulle
Full pryuely eke a fynche coude he pulle
And if he fonde ān wher a good felawe
He wold teche hym to haue none awe
In suche cas of the Archedecons curs
But if a mannes soule were in hise purs
For in his purs he shuld punysshed be
Purs is the Archedecons helle qᵈuod he
But weel I wote he lyed right in dede
For cursyng aught eche gylty man todrede
For curs wole sle like as assoylyng saueth
And also ware hym of a Significauit
In daunger had he at his owen̄ gyse
The yong gyrles of the diocyse
And knew her coūnsel and what was all her rede
A garlond had he set on hise hede
Als grete as it were for an ale stake
A bokeler had he made hym of a cake
With hym ther rode a gentil pardon̉ere
Of Rouncyuale hise frende and hise compẻre
That streyt was come fro the court of Rome
Ful lowde he song come hedre my love to me
This somynoᵘur bare to hym a styf burdon̄
Was neủer trompe of half so gret a son
This pardon̉ere had heer as yelwe as wex
But smothe it hyng as dooth a stryke of flax
By ounces hewge hise lokkꝭes that he hadde
And ther with hise shuldres he oủere spradde
But thynne it lay by culpons one and one
But hood for Iolyte wered he none
For it was trussed vp in his walet
Hym thought he rode all on the newe Iet
On coủered saf his cap he rode all bare
Suche glaryng eyne had he as an hare
A vernycle had he sewed vp on his cappe
Hise walet by forn hym was in his lappe
Fret full of pardon come fro Rome all hote
A voys he had as smal as a gote
No berde ne had he ne neủer shuld haue
As smothe it was as it were late shave
I trowe he wer a geldyng or a mare
But of hise craft from Berwyk in to ware
Ne was ther suche an other pardon̉ere
For in his male he had a pylwe bere
Whiche that he said was our ladye vayl
He seid he had a gobbet of the seyl
That seynt peter had whan that he wente
Vpon the see tyl IħuIhesu cryst hym sente
He had a croyse of latoūn full off stones
And in a glas he had pygges bones
And with these relikes whan þat he fonde
A pore person duellyng vp on londe
Vp on a day he gat hym more moneye
Than the ꝑperson gat in monethes tweye
